job.title: Property Claims Handler
job.description:
Full job description

Property Claims Handler

Location: Chelmsford

Salary: £33,000 – £40,000 depending on experience, plus performance-related bonus

Are you an experienced Property Claims Handler looking for a role where you can make a genuine difference to customers?

We’re working with an established insurance business in Chelmsford that is looking for a customer-focused and organised Property Claims Handler to join its team. This is an opportunity to take ownership of property claims from initial notification through to settlement, ensuring every claim is investigated thoroughly, handled fairly and managed in line with policy terms.

You'll be joining a business that places real importance on customer care, professional service and achieving fair outcomes, recognising that making an insurance claim can often be a stressful experience.

The Role

You'll manage a varied caseload of property claims, working closely with policyholders, contractors, surveyors and other third-party specialists to ensure claims progress efficiently and customers are kept informed throughout.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Managing claims from first notification of loss through investigation, assessment and settlement.
  • Reviewing policy coverage and investigating the circumstances of each claim.
  • Gathering information and assessing damage, repair estimates, invoices and associated costs.
  • Coordinating with loss adjusters, surveyors, contractors and other specialists where required.
  • Assessing claims and agreeing settlements within your authority, escalating more complex matters when necessary.
  • Maintaining accurate claims records, reserves and diary updates, ensuring outstanding actions are followed up promptly.
  • Identifying potential fraud indicators and pursuing recoveries where appropriate.
  • Managing customer expectations and ensuring policyholders receive a fair, supportive and professional service.
  • Recognising vulnerable customers and potential complaints, ensuring these are handled appropriately.
  • Working collaboratively with colleagues and third parties to support positive customer outcomes.

About You

We're looking for someone with experience in insurance claims handling, ideally with a background in property claims, who can combine technical knowledge with a strong customer-focused approach.

You'll also bring:

  • A good understanding of insurance policies and claims assessment.
  • Strong investigative skills, with the ability to analyse information and make informed decisions.
  • Excellent attention to detail and accurate record-keeping.
  • Confident communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to manage customer expectations.
  • A well-organised approach to managing a varied caseload and prioritising deadlines.
  • Empathy, sound judgement and a commitment to treating customers fairly.
  • The confidence to recognise potential issues and escalate claims when appropriate.
  • A proactive attitude and the ability to work effectively as part of a team.

A relevant insurance or financial services qualification would be beneficial but isn't essential if you have the right experience. Support with further professional development and relevant qualifications is available.

What's on Offer?

Alongside a salary of £33,000 – £40,000, depending on experience, plus a performance-related bonus, you'll benefit from:

  • A four-day working week – enjoy a better work-life balance.
  • Generous annual leave – 23 days' holiday plus bank holidays.
  • Strong pension contributions – an enhanced employer pension contribution of 6–8%.
  • Enhanced family leave – a supportive approach to family commitments.
  • Company celebrations – summer and Christmas parties.
  • Professional development – opportunities to build your technical knowledge and gain relevant qualifications.

Interested?

If you're an experienced claims professional looking for your next opportunity within a business that values customer care, professional development and a healthy work-life balance, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more!

job.title: Regulatory Monitoring & Enforcement Manager
job.description:
Our client, an established regulatory organisation, is seeking a proactive and analytical Regulatory Monitoring & Enforcement Manager to join its team.

This is an opportunity for someone from a legal, regulatory, audit, compliance or investigations background to take on a varied role with real responsibility.

The position combines regulatory monitoring and practice management with a particular focus on disciplinary investigations and enforcement. You will take ownership of the disciplinary process, coordinating cases, assessing evidence, supporting colleagues and progressing investigations through to adjudication, alongside managing a portfolio of regulated practices.

Key Responsibilities

Disciplinary Investigations & Enforcement

  • Oversee and coordinate disciplinary investigations and enforcement cases, ensuring matters are progressed efficiently.
  • Assist with the triage and assessment of potential disciplinary cases, identifying appropriate allegations and drafting supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate input from colleagues, including gathering evidence, preparing witness statements and compiling hearing bundles.
  • Manage case progression, identify outstanding actions, monitor deadlines and ensure cases keep moving forward.
  • Liaise with counsel, opposing counsel and other relevant parties, including providing instructions and supporting the preparation of cases for adjudication.
  • Provide advice, guidance and practical support to colleagues throughout the investigation and enforcement process.

Regulatory Monitoring & Practice Management

  • Manage a portfolio of regulated practices, acting as the main point of contact for queries, self-reports, submissions, complaints and other communications.
  • Plan and undertake monitoring inspections, including taking the lead on complex and large-scale inspections where required. Some travel will be necessary.
  • Identify potential regulatory breaches through monitoring reconciliations, accountants' reports and other tools, making recommendations and ensuring appropriate remedial action.
  • Prepare accurate monitoring reports and deliver feedback to practices, including communicating difficult or adverse findings.
  • Assist with the investigation, assessment and determination of claims and complaints, and participate in intervention activities when required.

AML, Reporting & Process Improvement

  • Undertake AML reviews and assessments, maintaining accurate records and ensuring potential money laundering concerns are escalated appropriately.
  • Keep up to date with relevant AML legislation and regulatory developments.
  • Review existing monitoring, inspection and disciplinary processes, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Contribute to improved procedures, guidance and working practices, preparing reports and analysis to support regulatory decision-making.

What We're Looking For

  • A background in law (a legal qualification would be desirable), regulation, compliance, audit or investigations.
  • Experience of investigations, disciplinary proceedings, litigation, enforcement or regulatory case management is essential.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to assess evidence, interpret information and identify key issues.
  • Excellent written skills and the ability to draft clear, accurate and well-structured allegations, reports and formal documents.
  • Confidence in managing challenging situations, having difficult conversations and delivering adverse news professionally.

What's on Offer

  • £50,000–£65,000 salary, depending on experience.
  • Hybrid working.
  • 30 days annual leave.
  • Opportunity to take ownership of and help develop the disciplinary and enforcement function.

If you're from a legal, regulatory or investigations background and are looking for an opportunity to take the lead, develop your experience and make a real impact, we'd be keen to hear from you.

job.title: Digital Marketing Manager
job.description:
About the opportunity

WE Talent is recruiting for a creative agency based in Leigh-on-Sea that is looking for a hands-on Digital Marketing Manager to join its team.

Working across a varied portfolio of clients and sectors, you'll take ownership of SEO and Google Ads, developing and delivering strategies that improve search visibility, drive website traffic and generate measurable results.

You'll work alongside specialists across digital, creative, branding, social media and web, combining analytical skills with creative thinking to deliver effective digital campaigns for clients.

The role

You'll be responsible for developing and implementing digital marketing strategies, with a particular focus on organic and paid search performance. This will include developing SEO strategies covering technical SEO, on-page optimisation and content, as well as creating, managing and optimising Google Ads campaigns.

You'll conduct keyword research and competitor analysis, identify opportunities to improve search performance, and plan, write and optimise blogs, website content and landing pages. You'll also manage client websites through WordPress and use Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Search Console and Google Tag Manager to monitor performance and identify opportunities for improvement.

You'll track leads, conversions, acquisition costs and return on marketing spend, translating client objectives into practical strategies and campaign plans. You'll prepare performance reports, communicate recommendations clearly to clients and collaborate with colleagues across social media, creative, brand and web to deliver joined-up campaigns. Using AI tools effectively for research, analysis, content creation and everyday digital marketing tasks will also be an important part of the role.

About you

We're looking for an experienced digital marketing professional with at least three years' experience, ideally within an agency or a similarly varied environment. You'll have strong, demonstrable experience in SEO and Google Ads, alongside practical WordPress experience and the ability to write and optimise website content and blogs.

You'll have a good working knowledge of GA4, Google Search Console and Google Tag Manager, together with strong analytical skills and the ability to turn data into practical insights and recommendations. You'll understand lead generation, conversions, cost per acquisition (CPA) and return on advertising spend (ROAS/ROMS), and be confident managing multiple client accounts and priorities.

You'll also be comfortable working directly with clients, explaining your recommendations and demonstrating the results of campaigns you've personally delivered. Experience using AI tools within digital marketing workflows is essential.

Additional experience

Experience with Meta Ads, other paid social platforms, organic social media, email marketing, CRM and marketing automation would be beneficial. Knowledge of AI and generative search, LinkedIn advertising, lead generation and conversion rate optimisation would also be useful.

The role would suit someone with an interest in editorial planning, content strategy and creative campaigns, as well as experience briefing web developers, designers, videographers or photographers. Experience contributing to new business proposals and pitches, or knowledge of web coding languages and UI/UX, would also be an advantage.

job.title: Design and Engineering Manager
job.description:
We're working exclusively with RADIX to recruit a Design and Engineering Manager, a key appointment as the business continues to grow and develop its design capability.

Working alongside its existing engineering consultants, this is an opportunity to establish and lead the design function, combining hands-on geotechnical and structural engineering with the freedom to shape technical standards, build a team and develop design into a commercial service.

RADIX is looking for someone who wants to make a genuine contribution to a growing business, take ownership of an important part of its future and grow with the company. For the right person, there is potential to progress into a wider leadership role, including the possibility of board-level involvement.

What the role involves:

  • Designing screw pile foundations for renewable energy, infrastructure and building projects, including geotechnical and structural checks, load testing and durability.
  • Producing and signing off complete design packages, including calculations, specifications and construction-ready drawings.
  • Interpreting ground investigation data and load test results to inform design decisions and optimise foundation solutions.
  • Setting technical standards and developing RADIX's design philosophy, calculation templates, reports and procedures.
  • Taking the technical lead with clients, their engineers and independent checkers, while supporting site teams with design queries.
  • Developing the design team, initially working alongside engineering consultants and recruiting additional expertise as the function grows.
  • Developing design as a commercial service in its own right, including helical pile design for both supply-only and supply-and-install clients.
  • Working with the Managing Director and leadership team on technical strategy, pricing and opportunities to grow the business across the UK and Europe.

What we're looking for:

  • A degree in civil, structural or geotechnical engineering, with typically eight or more years' relevant design experience, including checking the work of others.
  • Strong geotechnical judgement, including interpreting ground investigation data, selecting design parameters and designing piles to Eurocode 7.
  • Structural design experience to Eurocode 3, including bolted and welded connections, alongside experience specifying and interpreting pile load tests.
  • A hands-on approach, with the ability and willingness to produce calculations, design packages and construction drawings personally.
  • Experience explaining design decisions with clients and independent checkers, supported by clear technical writing skills.
  • Chartered Engineer status (CEng MICE or MIStructE), or actively working towards chartership with a clear plan.
  • Experience in piling, foundations, ground engineering or temporary works design would be advantageous. Screw pile or helical pile experience is useful but not essential.
  • Experience with FEA software such as SolidWorks Simulation, Ansys or similar, particularly in assessing structural components, fabricated products and connections, would be beneficial.
  • Experience establishing design procedures, technical standards or developing a small team would also be valuable.

Above all, RADIX is looking for someone who combines sound engineering judgement with an entrepreneurial mindset. You'll be comfortable getting into the technical detail while also spotting opportunities, taking ownership and helping build something for the long term.

RADIX can teach you about their product; they're looking for someone who brings the engineering expertise, initiative and ambition to help shape what comes next.

job.title: Compliance Administrator
job.description:
WE Talent are working with a busy, dynamic City of London organisation within the legal and regulatory sector seeking an experienced Compliance Administrator (Vetting & Regulatory Screening) to join their team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a candidate with a background in compliance, governance, regulatory operations or business screening to join a fast-paced, detail-driven environment.

The role focuses on statutory-style vetting and regulatory screening of businesses, including KYC checks, application processing, and eligibility assessments.

You will manage your own caseload, handle complex enquiries, and support structured decision-making processes within a regulated framework.

This is a varied, autonomous role requiring strong attention to detail, the ability to manage a high-volume workload, and confidence working within defined processes.

What you’ll be doing

As a key member of the team, your responsibilities will include:

  • Processing incoming telephone and email enquiries relating to registration, training, education, licensing, and compliance matters
  • Managing a personal caseload of applications, amendments, and regulatory screening/vetting cases
  • Carrying out a variety of screening checks, including KYC (Know Your Client), using multiple systems and databases
  • Assessing and processing applications in line with statutory and regulatory requirements
  • Handling general enquiries and providing clear, accurate guidance to applicants and stakeholders
  • Supporting adjudication panel activity when required, including preparation of case information
  • Supporting compliance and regulatory projects alongside core caseload responsibilities
  • Assisting with the coordination and administration of meetings and stakeholder interactions where needed (kept light and supportive rather than core focus)
  • Working closely with internal teams to ensure accurate, consistent and timely processing of cases

Who we’re looking for

We’re seeking an experienced, proactive compliance or regulatory professional who is comfortable working in a structured, process-driven environment with a complex and varied workload.

Essential experience and skills:

  • Experience in compliance, governance, regulatory operations, audit, business screening / vetting, or similar structured decision-making environments
  • Strong experience managing a high-volume caseload with accuracy and autonomy
  • Experience carrying out KYC and screening checks across multiple systems
  • Ability to assess information, follow regulatory processes, and work within defined frameworks
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including handling formal correspondence
  • Excellent attention to detail with a methodical, process-driven approach
  • Ability to work at pace in a complex and changing environment
  • Confident handling sensitive information with discretion and professionalism
  • Strong IT skills (Outlook, Word, Excel – intermediate), experience with case management systems advantageous
  • Understanding of compliance principles, data protection, and confidentiality requirements
  • Background in regulated environments involving statutory or quasi-statutory screening or decision-making highly beneficial

What’s on offer

  • 30 days annual leave plus bank holidays
  • Vitality healthcare scheme
  • Auto enrolment pension
  • Hybrid working option after training
  • 35-hour week
  • Wellness room and games room

This role is perfect for someone who enjoys variety, autonomy, and a busy, high-responsibility environment, with opportunities to work across both routine processes and project-based initiatives.

If you are confident, organised, and thrive in a busy, fast-moving role – apply now!

Suitable for: Compliance Administrators (business rather than personal), Compliance Officers, Governance Professionals, Quality Assurance Specialists, Case Handlers

Accounts & Finance
